answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing jobs that counterparties verify, with a small stake locked until the work passes review. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting into a hundred accounts does not multiply trust: each must win real jobs and risk its own stake. The kernel of the rule is costly repetition, not a pigment of reputation or a raven-like badge; an attacker must fund many deposits and produce verifiable work, while failed or colluding accounts lose stake and credibility.
